stem:
Tejas uses long division for $11 \div 4$. After the ones place he has remainder $3$ and wants to continue into decimals.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Regroup the remainder $3$ ones as $30$ tenths, continue dividing, and place the decimal point in the quotient when ones are regrouped into tenths.
Stop with remainder $3$ as the finished answer.
Continue writing digits after the ones place with no decimal point in the quotient.
Use the same tenths-regrouping plan when the remainder at the ones place is already $0$.

teacher.key_rationale: Leftover 3 ones become 30 tenths; the decimal point enters the quotient when ones are regrouped into tenths. Stopping at 'remainder 3' substitutes the remainder label for the decimal plan. Omitting the decimal point drops the place-value condition. Regrouping when the remainder is already 0 is outside this case.
